key_insight: EpNet learns an empirical pseudopotential that predicts complete electronic band structures directly from atomic coordinates across 63 elements in the s, p and d blocks.
engineering_relevance: Fast band-structure prediction could accelerate screening for electronic and optical materials at about 1% of DFT cost.
method: Use an equivariant neural network to construct a Hamiltonian from local potentials and nonlocal projectors.
Train solely on band energies rather than DFT-derived Hamiltonians.
Predict band structures without costly self-consistent DFT iterations.
evidence_signal: On 600,000 structures from an independent database, the abstract reports overall band-gap errors less than half those of existing models.
watch_item: The abstract leaves numerical errors on unseen chemical systems as unresolved placeholders, limiting assessment of absolute accuracy and transferability.
paper_title: Learning Electronic Band Structures Across the s, p, d Blocks with an Empirical Pseudopotential Network
